svg.title: A nonabelian symmetry distinguishes an inclusion from its dual
svg.desc: For an outer S3 action, Q is the fixed factor, P the original factor, T its crossed product. Both successive indices are six. The first higher algebra of Q inside P is C plus C plus M2, which is noncommutative. That of P inside T is C to the sixth power, which is commutative. Correct reflected endpoints reconstruct the original and dual inclusions separately.
svg.text: Index six does not fix the pair
An outer action of S₃ on the hyperfinite factor
Q = P^S₃ ⊂ P ⊂ T = P ⋊ S₃
Original pair Q ⊂ P
First higher algebra: Q′ ∩ T = C[S₃]
C ⊕ C ⊕ M₂(C) — noncommutative
Central trace weights: 1/6, 1/6, 2/3
Dual pair P ⊂ T
T₁ = M₆(P), P′ ∩ T₁ = C⁶
Six scalar blocks — commutative
Trace weights: 1/6 on each block
An isomorphism extends through the Jones tower.
An anti-isomorphism takes the opposite algebra.
Both preserve commutativity: these pairs differ.
Two reflected endpoints
Original N ⊂ M → M₁′ ∩ M∞ ⊂ M′ ∩ M∞
Dual M ⊂ M₁ → M′ ∩ M∞ ⊂ N′ ∩ M∞
Each arrow is a trace-preserving anti-isomorphism
from a generating tunnel at finite depth.
Propositions 41.1–41.2; Theorem 41.4; Corollary 41.5
